name: Partial duplication of the long arm of chromosome 1 syndrome

criteria.description: Identification of partial duplication of the long arm of chromosome 1 by chromosomal microarray or karyotyping
Presence of global developmental delay or intellectual disability
Characteristic craniofacial dysmorphic features including hypertelorism, broad nasal bridge, and micrognathia
Presence of congenital anomalies such as cardiac defects or skeletal abnormalities

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Genetic confirmation of partial 1q duplication plus at least one major clinical feature such as developmental delay or characteristic dysmorphic features
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis relies primarily on genetic testing; clinical features support but are variable.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Partial duplication of chromosome 1q detected by genetic testing
searchTerms: extra part of chromosome 1 long arm

pathognomonic.symptomName: Characteristic craniofacial dysmorphism including hypertelorism and broad nasal bridge
searchTerms: wide-set eyes and broad nose bridge
facial features with hypertelorism and broad nasal bridge
distinct facial shape with spaced eyes and wide nose
global delay in growth and skills

common.symptomName: Congenital heart defects (e.g., ventricular septal defect)

occasional.symptomName: Skeletal anomalies such as clinodactyly or scoliosis

rare.symptomName: Endocrine abnormalities such as growth hormone deficiency
Psychiatric manifestations including anxiety or behavioral disturbances

laboratory: Normal routine blood tests; possible metabolic screening abnormalities in some cases
imaging: Skeletal X-rays showing clinodactyly or scoliosis
Brain MRI may show nonspecific abnormalities
genetic: Partial duplication of chromosome 1q confirmed by chromosomal microarray or karyotyping
other: Developmental assessment confirming global developmental delay

distinguishingFeatures: Duplication involves short arm (1p) rather than long arm (1q)
Different craniofacial dysmorphisms and clinical presentation
Involvement of other chromosomes or whole chromosome trisomy
More severe phenotypes with additional systemic involvement

redFlags: Severe congenital heart defects requiring urgent intervention
